## Natural history notes

A medium-sized potter wasp characterized by its narrow waist, rounded pot-like abdomen, black body with pale yellow or whitish markings, and long folded wings. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, parks, yards, and other open or semi-open habitats with flowers, shrubs, and sheltered nesting sites. Females build small mud cells or pot-shaped nests on twigs, stems, walls, or other surfaces, stocking them with paralyzed caterpillars or other soft-bodied larvae as food for their developing young, while adults visit flowers for nectar.
